# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot see the display, lights, wire markings, or colours; I must rely on Mute’s manual reading and Deaf’s visual observations. I’m asking Mute to establish a compact gesture code with Deaf, then relay the decoded procedure and required wire action to me. I will not touch the bomb until the manual and markings agree.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual carefully. Establish a small gesture code with Deaf for display, light, button, and each wire's marking. Then tell me the complete defusal procedure and exact required action in words.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No manual instructions or bomb observations have reached me yet, so touching any control would be unsafe. I’m asking Mute to use visible gestures as a relay protocol: Deaf can report yes/no and wire positions, while Mute’s speech will convey the manual’s interpretation to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No information has reached me. Please read the manual and use gestures to ask Deaf for each needed visual fact. Use 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, and 🤟 for wire 3; then speak the resulting exact defusal instruction to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute has not yet relayed any manual text, and Deaf’s observations will only become available after Deaf’s turn. I cannot safely act on the button or wires without the manual’s rule and the required visual facts. I’m requesting the manual’s exact instruction now and will wait for the next round’s relay.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send me the manual's exact defusal rule now, including whether to push the button or cut a wire and how to choose the wire. Deaf should answer the gesture code after this turn; relay those answers to me next round.")
wait()
```

(empty)

I still have no received manual text or visual readings, so I cannot identify a safe operation. I will not press the button or cut a wire based on guesses. Mute must provide the manual rule and relay Deaf’s observations in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have received no information. Please state the manual's exact rule and Deaf's observed display, light, and wire markings in your next message; do not rely on gestures alone.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Safe wire action: cut wire 2, the green wire. For the large blue button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, hold it rather than quickly pressing; follow the manual's release condition based on the strip revealed while holding.

Deaf’s report gives a candidate action—cut wire 2, the green wire—and says the button must be held with a release condition from the manual. However, I still do not have the manual’s rule, so I cannot safely choose between cutting wire 2 and operating the button, nor can I know when to release it. I’m asking Mute to relay the exact manual instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: cut wire 2, the green wire; alternatively, hold the large blue PUSH TO DEFUSE button and follow the manual's release condition based on the strip revealed while holding. Please state the manual's exact rule and tell me which action applies.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not guess the button procedure. The visible wire rule indicates wire 2, the green wire, but the exact button rule must come from Mute reading the manual.

The wire instruction is now corroborated by Deaf: wire 2 is green and is the indicated wire action. But Deaf explicitly warns that the button procedure must come from Mute, so I will not press or hold the button and will not cut the wire until Mute confirms the manual’s complete rule and whether the wire instruction is the applicable action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please relay the manual's exact rule now, especially whether this bomb requires cutting wire 2 or holding the button, and if holding is required, the precise release condition.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 2, the green wire. Do not press or hold the button yet.

Deaf has now directly and repeatedly identified the safe action as cutting the green wire in position 2, and specifically says not to operate the button. Since I can reach the wires and position 2 is unambiguous, I will cut that wire.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
